claim_one_line: ONE TICK OR TWO ACTS: THE ADVISOR SEAT'S SEALED RUN VERIFIED ON MAIN, AND WHAT THE TICK DOES TO THE WEAVE'S THREE (P-769; data-free, integers and SnapPy; the seat's code not run): the seat's result holds in every part. With n letters, n = 1 to 12, there are 0 1 2 3 6 9 18 30 56 99 186 335 two-act histories and the tick adds 1 1 1 2 3 5 9 16 28 51 93 170 with an odd number of runs, about half as many again. Of the 69 two-act histories with at most 8 letters, 11 are their own mirror image (five are a tick history done twice, six by a reflection) and 58 lie in 29 mirror pairs, by the law of B1867 and by SnapPy on 69 of 69. The 22 tick histories of an odd number of runs with at most 7 letters are all non-orientable and each has the same history done twice as its orientation cover. The group of the moves mod N doubles with the exchange at N = 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and not at 2. At level 5 the tick multiplies the points of the golden line by 3, exchanging the two lines the record treats as a choice; one tick fixes and inverts no non-trivial fibre character, two invert the group of order 5. A single tick alone has the golden direction; L, R and the bare exchange alone have rational ones. Main adds: on the weave's six-dimensional space the exchange carries the triplet into its conjugate, the two acts' 96 matrices leave two pieces and the 192 with the exchange leave one, so the tick gives the three no hand -- it joins the two hands. Nothing forbids the tick and nothing forces it; whether it is an act is the owner's to rule (P-771), with three debts named first. 0 of 19.
